title: Metric choice — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, a teammate wants a log line for every latency sample. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud why a log line per latency sample is the wrong instrument, and propose what to record instead.

vocabulary.meaning: choosing between a log, a metric, and a trace according to the question to be answered, not according to habit
the storage and processing a signal consumes per event, which decides whether it can be recorded for every request

expectedElements: The question each signal answers is distinguished
The per-event cost is used as the deciding argument
A concrete alternative instrument is proposed
modelAnswer: A log line per latency sample is the wrong instrument, and the reason is cost per event rather than taste. A log line is a stored, searchable record; at one per request that is millions of records a day whose only use is to be aggregated. A metric answers the same question at a fraction of the storage, because it aggregates at write time. The trade is that a metric cannot tell you which request was slow, only that some share was. So I would record latency as a metric, and keep logs for the requests that exceed a threshold. That gives both the distribution and the individual examples as evidence. What threshold would be useful to you?
commonMistakes: Choosing the instrument by habit rather than by cost per event
Replacing logs with metrics without keeping any way to find a slow request
variants: Answer again when the teammate says storage is cheap.
